title: llama.cpp MoE Offload: --n-cpu-moe vs the New Expert Cache (Developers Digest, no author named, 9 Oct 2026) relaying llama.cpp PR #29887 'llama : add a GPU cache for MoE experts kept in host memory' (author am17an, opened 3 Oct 2026, merged 7 Oct 2026) and PR #30112 (multi-GPU, merged 8 Oct 2026)
id_read: blog HTML (curl) + GitHub API JSON of PR #29887 body, its 64 comments, PR #30112 body; no arXiv
setup: Model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4_0, 93.7 GiB total, 65.4 GiB experts (blog calls it 125B params, ~6B active; arch string in a comment 'qwen4exp'). EPYC 7742, 16 threads, one NUMA node, PCIe 4.0 x16, experts in HOST RAM (not disk), llama-server -fa on -c 32768 -b 2048 -ub 2048 -t 16, temp 0, no MTP. Benchmark: SPEED-Bench 'qualitative', 11 categories x 3 samples, --osl 512, concurrency 1 (single-GPU table, PR #29887); 1 sample/category = 11 prompts (2x4090, PR #30112). Baseline = master with default --fit (no cache). Cache = per-layer-bank LRU of experts in VRAM, only misses uploaded; applies only to ubatch <= 32 (decode); hit stats counted separately for ubatch<=8 (decode) and >8.

numbers.what: RTX 4090 decode, --fit --moe-cache-mib 6544 (10.4 GB layers + 6.4 GB cache)
RTX 5090 decode, -cmoe + 19000 (18.6 GB cache = 28.4% of 65.4 GiB experts)
Radeon AI PRO R9700 32GB, Ryzen 7 8700F, 32 GB RAM, Windows, -cmoe, DIFFERENT model (GSQ-RCO Coder IQ1_M, 24 GB experts): 8000 MiB (33% of experts) / 16000 MiB (67%)
Same box re-run at later commit
numbers.ratio: 1.01x / 1.97x (author: cache only breaks even with CPU path at 85% hit); all-on-GPU 43.3

numbers.what: RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, 62 GB RAM, UD-IQ3_XXS 78 GB (fork port)
numbers.where: blog, citing review thread (not re-read at source)

numbers.what: Offline LRU trace study on real Qwen3.8-Flash-Next routing (48 layers, 512 experts, 10 prompts, per-layer LRU)
numbers.where: PR comment by lich-77 7 Oct (single commenter, unverified)

numbers.what: GLM-5.3-Flash (288 experts, top-8) 1x RTX 5090 PCIe4, 10.5% cache
numbers.value: 14.23 / 12.9 tok/s, hit 47.0%, PCIe RX 24.7 GB/s avg

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: RTX 4090 decode 34.8 to 64.4 tok/s with -cmoe + 15000 MiB cache
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: True: 34.78->64.39 is TWO RTX 4090s (layer split), PR #30112, 15000 MiB per GPU, hit 95.8%. Single 4090 best row is 25.0->40.7 (1.63x) with 11000 MiB. First pass flagged this correctly.

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: simulated 8 GB card 11.0 tok/s no cache
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: 11.0 is a 32 GB R9700 with -cmoe on a different, tiny-quant model; 'simulated 8 GB card' is the catalog's gloss, not in the source. Blog says 'to simulate a smaller card'.
Numbers correct but 8000 MiB = 33% and 16000 MiB = 67% of that model's 24 GB of experts, not a small cache. Later re-run gave 11.9/23.2.

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: decode hit rates (truncated in catalog)

why: Speed: no. Experts sit in host RAM over PCIe 4.0 (24-32 GB/s), decode is GPU compute from a VRAM cache, a 4090/5090/R9700 is required, and the 2.2x needs a 18.6 GB cache plus 128+ GB host RAM. Hit-rate evidence: YES and important. This is the only source with real-routing hit rates for a 512-expert top-10 125B-class model (same family as our target): PR author 72% at 13% of host experts (--fit row: 6.4 GB of 48.9 GB host-resident), 77% at 16%, 89% at 28%; lich-77 offline per-layer LRU 75.9% at 14%, 87.6% at 25%. Caveat: workload mix (33 mixed prompts) and cold/warm state change hit by 10+ points (72% vs 85.9% at similar share in the 1-sample 2xGPU run).
quality_loss: Method is exact in principle (LRU cache only changes where experts are computed). But comments report greedy output diverging from the non-cache path in a port (antomicblitz) and a repetition loop ('the the the') with cache on in 4 of 4 runs on a 20k-word essay prompt (insunaa), unconfirmed, vanished after changing top-k; no benchmark of quality given.
ablation: Partial: cache vs --fit vs -cmoe vs tuned --n-cpu-moe are compared (so cache vs static placement is isolated: 1.01-1.05x vs tuned --n-cpu-moe on 3090). No layout/prefetch ablation. Policy: lich-77 offline LRU/FIFO/LFU/heat-decay; frequency-aware only wins below ~10% share, LRU best >=25%. Other commenters (Volunteer-1, pashko-k) claim LRU 'performs very poorly' without data.
limitations: Author/PR: batch <= 32 only; single device at first; blog: 'We have not run these configurations ourselves'; competes with whole expert layers for VRAM; prompt processing falls (0.73x); regressions: GLM-5.3-Flash 33->16 tok/s on 2 GPUs at 43.5% hit; break-even with CPU-only at ~85% hit on PCIe4 x8 (Volunteer-1 claims ~74% of experts cached).
contradicts_our_findings: YES, partly. pubtech E.md says hit 0.95/0.96 at 16/32 GB local caches and A/B.md map cache bytes to 'token footprints' on a 128-expert, top-8 Qwen3-30B trace. By my arithmetic (computed by me, not in sources) a 16 GB machine cache of 9.15 GiB = 3.6k experts = 14.8% of the 512x48 experts, whereas on the 30B proxy the same footprint count is 2911 of 6144 slots = 47%. Real-model hit at ~14% share is 0.72-0.77 (PR) / 0.76 (offline trace), not 0.95. At 32 GB (~41% share) interpolated real hit ~0.93 vs our 0.96 (close). At 8 GB (~4% share) real hit is probably under 0.6 (62% at 7.8%) vs our 0.56 at 2.07 footprints (13% share on proxy). Our 29%-share figures (0.856 dense / 0.789 4x-sparse) bracket real 0.876-0.89, fine.

id_read: arXiv 2402.07033 v3 (1 May 2025, 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025') and v1 (10 Feb 2024, preprint, authors Kamahori, Gu, Zhu, Kasikci) both read as PDF text
setup: Mixtral-8x7B 16-bit (>90 GB). v3 Table 1: Env 1 Quadro RTX 6000 24GB, PCIe3 x16 (32GB/s), Xeon Gold 6126 (48 cores), 56/256 experts on GPU; Env 2 RTX 6000 Ada 48GB, PCIe4 x16 (64GB/s), Xeon Platinum 8480+ (112 cores), 125/256 experts. v1: Env 2 was an L4 GPU. ShareGPT prompts. Baselines v3: DeepSpeed-MII 0.2.3 (ZeRO-Infinity), Mixtral-Offloading (extended to fp16, offload_per_layer 7 / 5), llama.cpp b2956 (ngl 8 / 16). Metrics: tok/s end-to-end (in 32-256, out 64-512), TTFT (in 512-4096), beam search width 4-16 (vs llama.cpp only). Software PyTorch, AVX512_BF16 CPU kernel. Experts in host RAM; no disk.

numbers.what: v3 single-batch end-to-end, average over 15 length configs x 2 envs
v3 appendix TTFT / ITL across baselines

numbers.ratio: as stated; >3 tok/s on a 24GB GPU

numbers.what: v3 hit rate from popularity placement, Env 1 (56/256)

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: 8.2x (Quadro RTX 6000) and 10.1x (L4) single-batch latency vs weight-swapping baselines
catalog_numbers_correct.correct: yes for v1 only; absent in v3
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: These are in arXiv v1 (10 Feb 2024): vs Mixtral-Offloading specifically, Env 2 = L4. v3/ICLR replaced them with 1.26x/1.30x/11.57x vs llama.cpp etc. and Env 2 = RTX 6000 Ada. The catalog URL (ar5iv) probably serves v1. First pass said 'wrong, possibly earlier version, unverified': confirmed earlier version.

why: GPU required; experts in host RAM and executed on the CPU with AVX512_BF16; fp16 model; the gain is that CPU compute beats PCIe weight copy at batch 1; with NVMe-resident weights and CPU-only there is no GPU to orchestrate. Cache share of experts is 22-49% on GPU, popularity placement adds only 3-4 points.
ablation: none for placement vs execution strategy, only the hit-rate calculation; sensitivity to datasets in App D.
limitations: Authors tested one main model plus Phi-3.5-MoE; baselines weak at batch 1; popularity profile assumed 'almost universal across datasets'.
contradicts_our_findings: No. 3-4 point gain of popularity-pinning over random agrees with our finding that offline hot lists are far worse than LRU (E.md: 0.30 vs 0.57 at 8 GB) in the sense that static placement gives little.

'Offloading baselines' conceals that HOBBIT replaces missed experts by int4/int2 copies (lossy, <=1 pt on 2 benchmarks).

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: figures only per model; averages as stated

why: HybriMoE: A6000 + kTransformers, host-RAM experts, 25-75% GPU cache ratio, 8-64 experts per layer. HOBBIT: closest regime (Jetson, NVMe) but the 18.9x/9.93x come from a baseline that page-faults (llama.cpp mmap on shared-memory Jetson) or a GPU-server design (MoE-Infinity), plus int2 substitution which is a quality change; on the RAM-rich 4090 it is 1.3x. MoE-Infinity: expert cache + prefetch in GPU with all experts in host RAM and large PCIe bandwidth. DAOP: A6000, Mixtral/Phi, expert substitution ('graceful degradation').
quality_loss: HOBBIT: <=1 pt on GSM8K/TruthfulQA (fp16 vs fp16+int4; int8 vs int8+int2) for 2 models (Table 3). DAOP: Table V/VI says minimal impact, GSM8K the exception (discussion section not read in detail). HybriMoE, MoE-Infinity: exact.

limitations: HOBBIT: prefetch useless in decode because of mispredict penalty; HybriMoE: scores stop mattering at 75% cache; MoE-Infinity: needs host RAM for the whole model.
contradicts_our_findings: No contradiction; HOBBIT's finding that decode prefetching gives ~1.01-1.05x agrees with our prefetch results.

title: LExI: Layer-Adaptive Active Experts for Efficient MoE Model Inference (Chitty-Venkata, Madireddy, Emani, Vishwanath; Argonne National Laboratory)
setup: Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, OLMoE-1B-7B-0924, MiniCPM-MoE, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny. 4x H100 80GB (2 for DeepSeek models), vLLM FusedMoE, tensor parallel, batch 16, throughput = (input+output tokens)/end-to-end latency. Method: per-layer perturbation (Frobenius norm of output change between top-k_base and top-k) on Gaussian random inputs (data-free), then an evolutionary search for per-layer k under a global budget B (sum of k). Baselines: inter-pruning NAEE 12.5/25/50% and intra-pruning (Yang et al.) 12.5/25/50%. Tasks: 9 LM-Eval (ARC-c/e, BoolQ, HellaSwag, MMLU, OBQA, RTE, WinoGrande), Qasper F1, passkey, perplexity C4/PTB/WikiText, VLM MME/MMMU/ScienceQA.

numbers.value: same throughput as 50% intra pruning, +10% accuracy; +15% vs 50% inter pruning
numbers.ratio: not a speedup over full k

numbers.value: at least +5.1% throughput vs both prunings, +0.5% accuracy
'same throughput on H100 with 10% better accuracy than traditional expert pruning'
numbers.where: Abstract (inconsistent with Sec 5 text, which gives the 10% to OLMoE)

numbers.value: ~2.4k throughput at ~23 ppl on C4; ~2.2k at ~10 ppl on WikiText
+6.5% throughput at equal accuracy vs inter pruning; +6 accuracy points vs intra
35.5 F1 at ~4.1k throughput vs inter 34 at ~3.9k, intra 30 at ~3.75k; +5.1-9.3% throughput

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: Static per-layer expert counts without retraining or data
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: data-free: only weights and random Gaussian input; evolutionary search.

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: first-pass: OLMoE matches 50% intra-pruning throughput with ~10% higher accuracy (Fig 4)
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: Sec 5 says OLMoE; the abstract attributes the 10% to Qwen1.5-MoE, internal inconsistency in the paper. 'Accuracy' units (points vs relative) not stated.

why: Idea (per-layer non-uniform k, chosen from weights alone) transfers; numbers do not: GPU H100, batch 16, all weights resident, throughput compared to pruned models rather than to the unreduced model, so the absolute speedup vs full top-k is not reported in any text table. The method reduces expert count per token and hence bytes per token in our setting, but the benefit there is untested. Search space k=1..k_base. No CPU or disk experiment.
quality_loss: Accuracy/perplexity 'close to the base model' per figures only (Fig 4-8); no table with deltas to full-k; Mixtral perplexity ~10 on WikiText at ~2.2k throughput (base value not in text).
ablation: none isolating anything relevant to cache/layout; the pruning-vs-top-k comparison is the only comparison
limitations: Does not reduce memory footprint (so little use when memory-bound); inapplicable if k_base=1 (Llama-4); can be combined with pruning.
contradicts_our_findings: Paper's claim that per-layer k gives 'negligible accuracy loss' is not tested at 125B and sits against our OLMoE k=4 result (+45.6% relative ppl); LExI never shows a uniform k=4 of 8 baseline, so no direct contradiction.

title: Certain Head, Uncertain Tail: Expert-Sample for Test-Time Scaling in Fine-Grained MoE (Chen, Wang, Zeng, Shao, Qiu, Li, Liu, Cheng; CAS/others; ICML 2026 proceedings, 43rd ICML)
setup: Table 1: Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, top-8), GPT-OSS-20B (32 experts, top-4), Ling-Lite-1.5 (64 experts, top-6), Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (table shows 256 experts, top-10; from memory the real model has 512 routed experts, so the table entry may be wrong or I mis-aligned the scrambled column). Benchmarks AIME-120/2024/2025, HMMT-2025, MATH500-Hard, GPQA-Diamond, LiveCodeBench-v6-Lite; LightEval 0.9.1 + vLLM 0.10.2 on 8x A800-80GB, tensor parallel 8. Overhead tests: random WikiText-2 prompts, prompt 1024, batch 8, output 1024 (Table 3); prefill 256-1024 x batch 1-32 (Tables 6,7).

numbers.value: floor(k/2)+1 or +2; below k/2 stability and exploration collapse

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: Greedy accuracy stays stable with activated experts halved
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: 'half' means k/2+1 (5 of 8 on Qwen3-30B, 6 of 10 on the 10-expert model), only on GPQA/AIME greedy, shown as a figure; no table value anywhere in the paper.

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: sampling-based metrics degrade more
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: pass@n falls at k/2+1 (Fig 2b), no number given in text

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: first-pass: speed table is overhead only (<1%)
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: Tables 3,6,7: ratios ~100% for batch 1-32

why: Evidence that halving active experts leaves greedy reasoning accuracy roughly intact on top-8 to top-10 fine-grained MoEs is directly on-topic for lowering bytes per token; but it is accuracy on GPQA/AIME only (not perplexity, long-form generation or tool use), at k/2+1 not k=4 of 10, GPU-served, and speed from smaller k is never measured. Our k=4 of 8 OLMoE perplexity +45.6% concerns a different metric.
quality_loss: Not measured numerically as a table; figure says negligible for greedy at k/2+1 (about 5/8 or 6/10 of the experts retained, i.e. 62%/60%, not 50%).
ablation: k_keep sweep (App B.1) on AIME-120 for Qwen3-30B and Ling-Lite: stable region k/2 <= k_keep < k; no speed ablation.
limitations: Authors discuss diversity/stability, not inference cost; the paper's own aim is test-time scaling, k reduction is a probe.
contradicts_our_findings: Weakly: suggests half-k keeps greedy accuracy, our OLMoE perplexity at k=4 says +45.6%; the two are different metrics and different models. See family #13 prior art arXiv 2609.04575 for the reconciliation (renormalisation gain).

title: MoDES: Accelerating Mixture-of-Experts Multimodal Large Language Models via Dynamic Expert Skipping (Huang, Wang, Yuan, Gong, Ding, Guo, Liu, Zhang; HKUST/Beihang/PKU; CVPR 2026)

title: Achieving Cloud-Grade SLOs for Local Mixture-of-Experts Inference through CPU-GPU Hybrid Design (Wang, Hou, Ji, Qu, Zhang; Tsinghua / Xingyun Integrated Circuits; accepted OSDI '26)
setup: Own platform: 2x AMD EPYC 9355, 24x DDR5-6400 48GB (1.15 TB, 1228 GB/s theoretical), 2x RTX 5090 32GB. DeepSeek-R1/V3 671B (INT4/Q4_K_M 404GB, FP8), Kimi-K2 1T, DeepSeek-V3.1. Baselines KTransformers (own platform measured; plus its published numbers cited), ik_llama.cpp, llama.cpp. Contributions: stream-loading prefill (SLP), distributed SLP, intra-node prefill/decode disaggregation, AVX-512 FP8 GEMV, fine-grained CPU parallelism.

why: 1 TB DDR5 across 24 channels, EPYC 9355 pair, 2x5090, DeepSeek-scale; decode is memory-bandwidth-bound from host RAM (28 tok/s needs ~hundreds of GB/s); prefill is compute-bound on GPU with weights streamed over PCIe. None of 8-32 GB RAM, NVMe, CPU-only batch 1. One useful general point: decode on large MoE is memory-bandwidth-bound and engines reach only ~50% of nominal bandwidth.
quality_loss: FP8 keeps quality (Table 2: within 0.3-0.8 pts of official); INT4 comparisons are about speed only; KT 'rerouted' model is called capacity-reduced.
ablation: Per-technique results (SLP vs AVX, DSLP vs SLP, kernel Table 1) but nothing on cache/layout/prefetch of experts from disk.
limitations: Authors: results cover a dual-socket, PCIe-attached commodity node; lower-end bandwidth/PCIe discussed in Sec 6 (not itemised).
